blocks.html: Technology changes very fast. Ten years ago, very few people paid using a phone; today a vegetable seller in Patna accepts UPI. Emerging trends are new technologies that are growing quickly and changing how we live, learn and work.
Artificial Intelligence is the ability of a machine to do tasks that normally need human intelligence, such as understanding language, recognising faces, solving problems and taking decisions.
Examples: Google Maps finding the fastest route, YouTube recommending videos, face unlock on a phone, chatbots on bank websites, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.
ML is a part of AI in which a computer learns from data instead of being given every rule. The more data it sees, the better it gets.
Example: An email spam filter learns from thousands of emails marked "spam" and "not spam", then decides for new emails by itself.
Types of ML:

items.html: Supervised learning: Learns from labelled examples (photos labelled "cat" or "dog").
Unsupervised learning: Finds groups in data without labels (grouping customers by shopping habits).
Reinforcement learning: Learns by trial and reward (a robot learning to walk, AI learning to play chess).

blocks.html: (b) Deep Learning uses artificial neural networks with many layers, inspired by the human brain. It powers face recognition, voice assistants and self-driving cars.

(c) Generative AI creates new content — text, images, music, code and video — from a prompt. Examples: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini (text), DALL·E and Midjourney (images). These are built on Large Language Models (LLMs) trained on huge amounts of text.

(d) Natural Language Processing (NLP) lets computers understand and produce human language. Examples: Google Translate (English ↔ Hindi), voice typing, Alexa, Siri, grammar checkers, sentiment analysis of reviews.
AI vs ML vs Deep Learning: Deep Learning ⊂ Machine Learning ⊂ Artificial Intelligence.

blocks.html: A robot is a machine that can sense its surroundings, process information and act, often on its own. Robotics combines mechanical engineering, electronics and computer science.

Examples: robotic arms in car factories, Mars rovers (NASA's Perseverance), Chandrayaan-3's Pragyan rover, surgical robots (da Vinci), delivery drones, robot vacuum cleaners, humanoid robots such as Sophia.
Big Data means data sets so large and fast-growing that normal software cannot store or process them. Example: the millions of UPI transactions that happen in India every hour.

rows: YouTube receives hundreds of hours of video every minute
Speed at which data is created
Live cricket score updates, stock market
Many types: text, images, video, sensor data
Amazon suggesting what to buy next

blocks.html: Data analytics is the process of examining data to find patterns and make decisions. Example: a cricket team analysing a batter's weak shots; a hospital predicting which months have more dengue cases.
IoT is a network of everyday devices (things) that have sensors and software and are connected to the internet, so they can collect and share data without human help.
Examples: smart watches, smart bulbs controlled by phone, smart door locks, FASTag at toll plazas, smart electricity meters, soil-moisture sensors for farmers.
Web of Things (WoT): Uses web technologies (HTTP, web browsers) to let IoT devices talk to each other and to users through ordinary web pages and apps.
Sensors detect changes in the environment and convert them into signals. Examples: temperature sensor, motion (PIR) sensor, light sensor, GPS, accelerometer, fingerprint sensor.

Smart cities use IoT and data to manage traffic, water, electricity, waste and safety. India's Smart Cities Mission includes cities such as Patna, Bhubaneswar, Pune and Surat, with features like smart traffic lights, CCTV surveillance and integrated command centres.
Cloud computing means using computing resources — storage, servers, software — over the internet instead of on your own computer. You pay only for what you use.
Examples: Google Drive, Gmail, Netflix, DigiLocker, Microsoft 365, AWS.

rows: A ready platform to build and run your own apps

blocks.html: Types of cloud: Public (anyone can use, e.g. AWS), Private (one organisation only), Hybrid (mix of both).
Real-life comparison: IaaS is like renting an empty flat; PaaS is like renting a furnished flat; SaaS is like staying in a hotel.
Grid computing connects many computers in different places so they work together as one large virtual supercomputer to solve a big problem.
Example: scientists split a large weather or medical research task into small parts and send each part to a different computer.

rows: Resources are provided as a service by one provider

blocks.html: A blockchain is a digital record (ledger) of transactions stored in blocks that are linked together in a chain and copied on many computers. Once a block is added, it cannot be changed without changing all blocks after it on every computer, so it is very secure.

items.html: Decentralised: No single owner controls it.
Transparent: Everyone in the network can see the records.
Secure: Uses cryptography (hashing).

blocks.html: Examples: cryptocurrencies (Bitcoin), supply-chain tracking, land records, digital certificates, voting systems.

items.html: Quantum computing: Uses qubits, which can be 0 and 1 at the same time (superposition). It can solve some problems, like drug discovery and code breaking, far faster than normal computers. India has a National Quantum Mission (2023).
5G: Fifth-generation mobile networks with very high speed and very low delay; supports self-driving cars and remote surgery.
Edge computing: Processing data near where it is created (on the device or a nearby server) instead of a distant cloud, for faster response.
3D printing: Builds solid objects layer by layer from a digital design.
Drones: Used for delivery, farming (spraying), mapping and disaster relief.

blocks.html: AI and IoT systems are made of simple decisions repeated very fast. These two small C++ programs show the idea. (You will learn if-else and loops in Chapter 6.)

blocks.code:
Bot: Hello! Ask me about the school. Type 'bye' to exit.
You: hello
Bot: Hi there! How can I help you?
You: what is the school time
Bot: School time is 8 AM to 2 PM.
You: bye
Bot: Goodbye! Have a nice day.

blocks.html: This bot follows fixed rules. A real AI chatbot such as ChatGPT or Claude instead learns language patterns from huge amounts of text, so it can answer questions it was never given a rule for.

blocks.code:
Enter room temperature (in C): 27
Fan speed: MEDIUM

blocks.html: In a real smart fan, the temperature comes from a sensor instead of the keyboard, and the program runs on a microcontroller such as an Arduino (which is programmed in a language based on C++).

blocks.html: 1. What is Artificial Intelligence? Give two examples.
Answer: AI is the ability of a machine to perform tasks that need human intelligence, such as understanding speech or making decisions. Examples: face unlock on phones, Google Maps route suggestions.
2. Differentiate between VR and AR.

rows: Adds virtual objects to the real world
Needs a headset; e.g. VR games
Works through a phone camera; e.g. Pokémon GO

blocks.html: 3. What is IoT? Give two examples.
Answer: The Internet of Things is a network of everyday devices fitted with sensors and connected to the internet so they can share data automatically. Examples: smart watch, smart electricity meter.
4. What is Generative AI?
Answer: Generative AI is a type of AI that creates new content such as text, images, music or code from a user's prompt. Examples: ChatGPT and Claude (text), DALL·E (images).
5. Name the three cloud service models with one example each.
Answer: IaaS — Amazon EC2; PaaS — Google App Engine; SaaS — Google Docs.
6. What is a sensor? Name two types.
Answer: A sensor is a device that detects a change in its surroundings (heat, light, motion) and converts it into an electrical signal. Examples: temperature sensor, motion sensor.
7. Differentiate between cloud computing and grid computing (two points).

Answer: Cloud computing provides resources as a paid service from a provider and is used by everyone; grid computing joins many separate computers to solve one large task and is used mainly in research.
8. What is edge computing?

Answer: Edge computing processes data close to where it is produced, on the device or a nearby server, instead of sending it to a distant cloud. This gives a faster response, e.g. in self-driving cars.
1. Explain Machine Learning and its three types with examples.
Answer: Machine Learning is a branch of AI where computers learn patterns from data and improve with experience, without every rule being programmed.

items.html: Supervised learning: Trained on labelled data. Example: predicting house prices from past sales; recognising handwritten digits.
Unsupervised learning: Finds hidden groups in unlabelled data. Example: grouping customers by buying habits.
Reinforcement learning: Learns by trying actions and getting rewards or penalties. Example: AI that learns to play chess or a robot that learns to walk.

blocks.html: 2. What is Big Data? Explain the 5 Vs.

Answer: Big Data is data so large, fast and varied that ordinary software cannot handle it. The 5 Vs are Volume (huge size), Velocity (speed of creation), Variety (text, video, sensor data), Veracity (accuracy) and Value (useful insights). See the table in 3.5 for examples.
3. What is a smart city? How do IoT and data help run it?
Answer: A smart city uses technology to improve services and quality of life. IoT and data help through:

items.html: Smart traffic: sensors and cameras adjust signals according to traffic.
Smart lighting: street lights switch on only when needed.
Water and power: smart meters detect leaks and track usage.
Waste management: bins with sensors tell trucks when they are full.
Safety: CCTV and command centres help police and emergency services.

blocks.html: India's Smart Cities Mission covers 100 cities, including Patna.
4. Explain blockchain technology and give three uses.

Answer: A blockchain is a shared digital ledger in which records are stored in blocks linked by cryptographic hashes and copied on many computers. It is decentralised, transparent and tamper-proof. Uses: (i) cryptocurrency such as Bitcoin, (ii) land and property records, (iii) tracking medicines or food in a supply chain, (iv) issuing digital certificates.

blocks.text: Very Long Answer Questions (10 marks each)

blocks.html: 1. (a) What is cloud computing? Explain IaaS, PaaS and SaaS with examples. (6) (b) State two advantages and two disadvantages of cloud computing. (4)

Answer (a): Cloud computing is the delivery of computing services — servers, storage, databases, software — over the internet on a pay-per-use basis. IaaS gives raw infrastructure like virtual machines (Amazon EC2); PaaS gives a platform to build and deploy apps without managing servers (Google App Engine, Replit); SaaS gives finished software in a browser (Gmail, Zoom). Comparison: renting an empty flat (IaaS), a furnished flat (PaaS), a hotel room (SaaS).
Answer (b): Advantages: data can be accessed from anywhere; no need to buy costly hardware. Disadvantages: needs a good internet connection; data privacy and security risks.
2. (a) Explain AI, Machine Learning, Deep Learning and NLP with one application each. (6) (b) Write a simple rule-based chatbot in C++ and explain how it differs from an AI chatbot. (4)

Answer (a): AI — machines doing intelligent tasks (Google Maps routing). ML — learning from data (spam filter). Deep Learning — multi-layer neural networks (face recognition). NLP — understanding human language (Google Translate).

Answer (b): See Program 3.1. The program checks the user's message against fixed rules (find("time") , find("fee") ). It cannot answer anything outside these rules. An AI chatbot is trained on a very large amount of text, learns language patterns and can answer new questions it was never programmed for.
3. Write short notes on: (a) Robotics (b) Quantum computing (c) 5G (d) Web of Things (e) 3D printing. (2 × 5)

Answer: See sections 3.4, 3.6 and 3.10. Key points: (a) machines that sense, think and act, e.g. Pragyan rover; (b) qubits and superposition, India's National Quantum Mission; (c) high speed, low delay mobile network; (d) using web technology to connect IoT devices; (e) making objects layer by layer from a digital design.
